steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a mixing bowl, combine the sweet potatoes, butter, egg yolks, brown sugar, salt, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and evaporated milk. Mix together well.
Beat egg whites until stiff peaks form; add 1/4 cup sugar and fold into sweet potato mixture.
Pour into pie shell and bake at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) for 10 minutes. Reduce heat and bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 30 minutes or until firm.

review.reviewBody: EXCELLENT! Very easy and tasty! For those of you who claimed that the filling was too "mooshy", try baking the potatoes in the oven and not boiling them. Baking them intensifies the flavor of the potatoes.

Other than the fact I pressure cooked the sweet potatoes, with just required liquid to cook. Used slotted silicone spoon to help drain and get out onto a plate. Then carefully tipping sideways to drain again. Changed the spices to short 2 tsp. of pumpkin pie spice instead. Didnt have ginger powder. Used condensed milk instead of evaporated. The baking difference was longer cook time. 45 minutes longer over the last 30. But, I slowly decreased oven temp, within that 45, upon checking wasn't set yet. 15 mins. past lowered to 325. Checked again after 10 mins. then lowered to 300, due to nice carmelation on top. I googled how to jazz up store bought crust. Melt 4 Tblsp. butter. Cool and add 1 tsp. vanilla and 1/2 tsp. rum. I melted the butter before making pie. Since it cooled quickly. Stir together gently. Brush the entire crust, just before filling. I made 2 pies and still had small bit of extras of the butter mix. Yes, this is "sweet" potato pie. Not overly sweet. Just delicious! Today, having a slice, I even sprinkled powdered sugar on top after gently warmed in microwave. As others have said, this is better than pumpkin!!

This came out perfect and delicious!!! I made it a little simpler and here's what I did: I microwaved the sweet potatoes for both ease and so that they wouldn't be watery. Since I wasn't at home and didn't have a mixer, I didn't bother with separating the eggs (none of the other recipes call for this). I used 1 1/8 cups of brown sugar and eliminated the white sugar. Finally, I used 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1 tsp of allspice. We loved it so much, I'm making it again the very next day!!!

This is a delicious recipe. I added 1 tsp of vanilla extract to the recipe. Also, I didn't have allspice so I added 1/2 additional tsp of cinnamon and nutmeg. I also baked my sweet potatoes instead of boiling them. That helps to retain the sweetness in the potatoes. It turned out very well.

This is a very good recipe. I've made it several times and have made a few discoveries: 1) bake your sweet potatoes - don't boil them. This makes for a more concentrated flavor. 2) puree them in the food processor - don't just mash them (my family doesn't like the fibrous texture when they're just mashed). 3) reduce the amount of sugar - I used 3/4 cup this last time. 4) Grate your own whole nutmegs, and use fresh ginger rather than the powdered stuff for a spicier kick.

Just made this pie last night and it was wonderful! Very light and fluffy and mmmmm good!
Only thing I did different is reduce the brown sugar to 1/2cup, and upped the spices from a 1/2 tsp to a full tsp. I also added allspice which gave it a wonderful flavor. I added 15 min to the baking time and it was perfect. Don't boil the potatoes, bake them. Boiling takes away from the flavor and will make your batter more mushy than firm.

Perfect sweetness without the 1/4 cup of added sugar into the egg whites. It is a family favorite with perfect flavor and texture . Ended up with 4 pies when I doubled the recipe (2X) . Had enough to share for Friendsgiving . Egg whites better than using corn starch . Made it the perfect texture .

Definitely my favorite sweet potato pie recipe ever! I make it with just a couple of modifications. If you're from the Deep South, you don't need to separate the eggs. It's even tastier when it's dense - instead of fluffy. You can also use 1/2 cup light brown sugar and 3/4 cup white sugar, instead of 1cp brown sugar to 1/4cp white sugar. As well, I squeeze in a half of real lemon (strained) to contrast the sweet taste. I also add alumuminum around the pie edges, before cooking, because I cook the pie for about 1.25 hours - to make sure it's cooked well and the color is burnt orange. Your pie should not look like it's golden. Next time, I'm gonna try it with half and half instead of evaporated milk. Regardless, this recipe will be your go to favorite.

I baked my potatoes and peeled them and put all the ingredients together while the potatoes were still warm. The whipped egg whites literally made the recipe spectacular. This recipe is a keeper. Only thing I added was a little bit of vanilla and I don’t like ginger so I left that out, but other than that, this recipe is perfect!

I replaced the ginger with a fourth as much of ground cloves because ginger = pumpkin pie to me (1/4 teaspoon for two pies, would be 1/8th for one) and halved the sugar. 1 cup of sugar total, 1/2 brown and 1/2 white

Doing this allowed me to replace my tried and true, modified and tested over the years, sweet potato pie recipe (lost in a move). Everyone loved it!

Note: Folding in the egg whites makes for a fluffier/higher pie which I learned a few years into making these for the holidays. So it's worth the trouble.

My only complaint is how long it took to set. Needed 15 extra minutes of baking total. Picture perfect when done.

I've made this recipe numerous times and I enjoy it every time. I think everyone makes each recipe their own. For myself I don't like a lot of sugar so I only added half a cup of brown sugar and omitted the white sugar. Also, I left the skins on the sweet potato, but blended it in my NutriBullet. This makes the pie super lite.

Great recipe!, albeit I baked the sweet potatoes (3) and used fresh ginger steeped with 1/4 cup hot water which was added to the milk. This was enough for 2 delicious pies!!! Thank you for the wonderful recipe!!!!! Next time, I’m going to substitute some cognac as suggested by another user. 🤤
I use 1/2c less brown sugar...i sprinkle 1/4 c or less brown sugar on the bottom of crust. Take out 2-3 T of condensed milk and add Brandy, Bourbon or Cognac (my fav).😋 😋 We prefer it cold!
Simple recipe and the pie came out perfect

I’ve made this multiple times and love how the egg whites create a lighter texture. Also, the combination of the brown sugar and granulated sugar. The only thing I do different is I roast my sweet potatoes rather than boil them.
Best sweet potato pie recipe!!! My Mom's recipe is good but my husband loves this one so much more. Thank you!!
